overall_summary: Bitcoin is holding near eighty-one point five thousand after the recent tech rout, with no clear break yet. Softer yields and a weaker dollar are supportive, but heavy ETF outflows and rising Middle East tensions are capping upside. Focus now turns to today's PMIs and next week's FOMC for the next catalyst.
key_points: BTC holds 81.5k after rout and liquidations
Yields plunge and DXY softens, risk-on tilt
Switzerland approves first retail spot Bitcoin ETF
Bitcoin ETFs see large outflows, October negative
Middle East risks rise on Iran and Houthi strikes

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs bleed $635M, October turns negative
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about 635 million dollars in net outflows on Thursday, the biggest single-day exit since late June. That snapped a three-day inflow streak of over a billion dollars and pushed October’s net flows back into the red by roughly 175 million. Traders should care because ETF flows have been a key demand signal; heavy redemptions, led by BlackRock’s IBIT and Fidelity, remove a cushion just as Bitcoin sits near key levels ahead of the Fed.
items.impact: Weaker institutional bid and near-term selling pressure on BTC

items.title: BTC holds near 81.5k after tech rout and liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin dipped toward 81,000 dollars Thursday as the Nasdaq plunged 2.6 percent on AI spending worries and oil climbed on Middle East tensions, then steadied near 81,500 to 81,700 on Friday. Crypto liquidations ran several hundred million dollars, mostly long positions. Traders care because BTC is testing the estimated cost basis of US spot ETF holders and the 50-day average right before next week’s FOMC; a hold keeps the range intact, a break opens lower supports.
items.impact: Range-bound chop until Fed or clear break of 80-82k zone

items.title: HSBC launches RedCoin stablecoin to 3 million users
items.summary: HSBC went live today with its first stablecoin, RedCoin, a Hong Kong dollar token available on the PayMe app used by more than 3.3 million people. Users can soon send it peer-to-peer and pay merchants, with plans later this year to buy tokenized investments. This matters because a major global bank is putting regulated stablecoin rails into everyday consumer payments, reinforcing institutional infrastructure beyond pure speculation.
items.impact: Positive for crypto adoption and stablecoin utility narrative

items.title: Switzerland approves first retail spot Bitcoin ETF
items.summary: Swiss regulator FINMA has cleared the country’s first spot Bitcoin ETF open to retail investors. BIT Asset Management’s BBIT fund is expected to start trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange in November and is currently Europe’s only true spot Bitcoin ETF structure. Traders should note the legitimacy boost and potential new European demand channel, even if initial volumes are modest compared with US products.
items.impact: Incremental positive regulatory and access catalyst for BTC

items.title: Ireland fines Coinbase 3.25 million euros on safeguards
items.summary: The Central Bank of Ireland fined Coinbase’s Irish e-money unit 3.25 million euros for failures in safeguarding customer funds and outsourcing oversight between 2020 and 2025. The firm admitted shortfalls in the designated account and heavy reliance on its US parent; no customers lost money and issues are said to be fixed. It is the second Irish hit on a Coinbase entity in a year, so traders watch for any broader European compliance overhang on the exchange.
items.impact: Limited direct BTC price effect; mild negative for Coinbase sentiment

items.title: Ethereum delays Glamsterdam testnet over security risks
items.summary: Ethereum developers postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade activation on the Hoodi testnet that had been set for October 26 after security researchers flagged gas-rule changes that could affect existing smart contracts. ChainSecurity cited multiple real-world examples; no new date is set and mainnet users are unaffected for now. This delays a capacity and efficiency upgrade that had been eyed for late 2026, so ETH traders face extended uncertainty on the roadmap.
items.impact: Short-term negative for ETH sentiment and upgrade timeline

items.title: US 10-Year Yields Plunge Nearly 19bps to Below 5%
items.summary: Treasury yields saw their biggest one-day drop since the 2023 banking crisis, with the 10-year falling about 17 to 19 basis points to around 4.95 or 4.96 percent. The move came as tech stocks sold off hard on AI funding and capex worries, sending investors scrambling into the safety of bonds. This eased some December Fed hike pricing and pulled the dollar lower. Crypto traders should care because lower yields reduce the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and often support risk appetite after a washout.
items.impact: Supports risk assets and BTC via easier financial conditions

items.title: Jobless Claims Fall to 194k Near Multi-Decade Lows
items.summary: Initial unemployment claims dropped to 194,000 last week, beating the 200,000 forecast and sitting near the lowest levels since the late 1960s. Continuing claims rose modestly to 1.728 million. This points to a still-tight labor market with very low layoffs even after soft September payrolls. Traders need to watch it because a resilient jobs market keeps the Fed on a hawkish bias and supports the case for holding or hiking rates, which can pressure risk assets if it hardens the higher-for-longer narrative.
items.impact: Reinforces strong economy but hawkish Fed lean

items.title: DXY Softens Toward 101.6-101.7 as Yields Retreat
items.summary: The US dollar index slipped to its weakest levels this month near 101.65 as Treasury yields collapsed and safe-haven flows favored the yen and Swiss franc. Markets remain cautious ahead of next week's FOMC with the Fed in blackout. A softer dollar is typically a tailwind for Bitcoin and other crypto by making dollar-denominated assets cheaper for foreign buyers and easing global liquidity conditions.
items.impact: Weaker USD supportive for crypto prices

items.title: FOMC Next Week: Hold Widely Expected, December Hike Priced
items.summary: Nearly all economists polled expect the Fed to keep the funds rate at 3.75 to 4.00 percent at the October 27-28 meeting, with a December hike now the base case for most. Officials are in blackout and recent hot inflation plus strong growth keep the door open for more tightening later. Crypto traders should care because the statement and press conference will set the tone for rates into year-end, directly affecting liquidity and risk appetite.
items.impact: Event risk; hold removes near-term hike fear but path remains hawkish

items.title: Flash PMIs and Final Michigan Sentiment Due Today
items.summary: S&P Global flash manufacturing, services and composite PMIs for October are due around 9:45 AM ET, expected to ease modestly from September's multi-year highs but stay firmly expansionary. Final University of Michigan consumer sentiment is set for 10 AM ET, expected around the preliminary 46.3 which marked a multi-month low with elevated inflation expectations. These give the freshest read on growth momentum and household confidence right before the FOMC. Strong prints could firm the dollar and yields while soft ones ease financial conditions further.
items.impact: Data will swing near-term rate expectations and USD

items.title: Eurozone PMIs Mixed as German Growth Softens, France Contracts
items.summary: German flash composite PMI fell to 52.8 from 53.8 while manufacturing held strong at 54.2; French readings slipped into contraction territory. UK composite and services beat expectations at 53.1. These paint a picture of uneven European recovery amid fiscal and political strains, with French yields hitting multi-decade highs. Global traders watch because weaker euro-area data can pressure the euro, support the dollar relatively, and influence cross-asset risk sentiment that spills into crypto.
items.impact: Mixed global growth signal; limited direct BTC catalyst

items.title: Iran Claims Seven Oil Tankers Hit in Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says four tankers were set ablaze during oil transfers and three more struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz overnight. Tehran threatens wider attacks on US bases if Washington keeps escorting ships. Oil prices climbed on the news as October already logs the highest shipping attacks since the war began. Traders should watch this closely because any real choke on Gulf crude would spike energy costs and hit risk assets hard.
items.impact: Higher oil prices and elevated geopolitical risk premium

items.title: US and Israel Plan Post-Midterm Strikes on Iran
items.summary: The New York Times and other outlets report US and Israeli militaries have drawn up detailed plans for a short, intense round of strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms. Targets include energy infrastructure, nuclear sites, and missile arsenals, with joint exercises already underway over Iraq. Trump has ruled out any attack before the vote. This keeps escalation risk hanging over markets and could drive oil higher once the election passes.
items.impact: Sustained oil upside and risk-off pressure post-election

items.title: Houthis Hit Saudi Airport; US Pulls Diplomats
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis struck King Fahd Airport in Dammam, killing two and injuring eight, after earlier hits on an oil field. The US State Department ordered non-essential embassy staff and families to leave Saudi Arabia amid the surge in attacks. Oil jumped as regional energy infrastructure stays under threat. Crypto traders need to track this because wider Gulf instability feeds directly into higher energy prices and broader risk aversion.
items.impact: Oil spike and Middle East risk premium rise

items.title: Putin Agrees to Resume Ukraine Peace Talks
items.summary: After meeting US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg, Putin said Russia is ready in principle for trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine around November 10, possibly in Abu Dhabi. Moscow released a long-held American detainee as a goodwill step, though fighting and strikes continue on both sides. Zelenskyy also backed early talks. A credible path to de-escalation would ease European energy and security fears and support risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Potential de-risking of Europe and lower war premium

items.title: Netanyahu Orders Full West Bank Lockdown
items.summary: After a shooting near Hebron wounded five Israelis and left two Palestinian suspects dead, Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered a cordon on Hebron and preparation for full closure of the West Bank. The move comes just days before Israel's October 27 election, which is already seen as highly consequential. Heightened West Bank tension adds another layer of Middle East volatility that markets will price into oil and risk sentiment.
items.impact: Adds local escalation risk ahead of Israeli election

items.title: Trump Says Musk Restored Ukraine Starlink Access
items.summary: President Trump claimed Elon Musk has put Ukraine's military Starshield service back online after reports of speed restrictions that crippled drone operations. The Wall Street Journal said Trump personally called Musk to demand the lift. Ukrainian officials counter that limits largely remain in place. The episode highlights ongoing friction over support for Kyiv and could sway battlefield momentum and related energy market moves.
items.impact: Mixed signals on Ukraine war logistics and US policy
